You juggle many tasks as a field service business. Whether you're fixing AC units, mowing lawns, responding to plumbing requests, or bidding on kitchen remodels, your ability to stay organized impacts your bottom line. From scheduling jobs to invoicing clients, it’s essential to keep your operations running smoothly so nothing falls through the cracks.

That’s why many service providers use software platforms to help manage administrative tasks and sales opportunities. Housecall Pro is one of the better-known names in the space, with tools that simplify business operations. However, depending on which features are more important to you — lower costs, better customization, streamlined scheduling, and more — there are several other companies like Housecall Pro worth considering.

Let’s start with what Housecall Pro offers and then explore six Housecall Pro competitors that could be an even better fit for your business.

What Is Housecall Pro?

Housecall Pro is a business management platform built for home service professionals. It serves businesses of all sizes, but it’s especially popular among small to mid-sized teams in HVAC, electrical, and cleaning services. Below are some of the key features that Housecall Pro offers.

Revenue Growth Tools

With Housecall Pro, businesses can manage reviews, use built-in website tools to boost online visibility, and capture incoming calls through a professional call answering service. The online booking system streamlines customer scheduling, and the pipeline dashboard helps teams track prospects at every stage.

Job Management

Drag-and-drop job assignment, calendar visibility, and real-time vehicle GPS tracking make scheduling and dispatch quick and easy. Built-in customer communication tools allow businesses to send job status updates through text or email. The platform supports quoting and proposals, and the mobile app keeps field techs moving.

Payment and Financing

Housecall Pro supports invoicing and payments, plus expense cards to track business purchases. For companies handling higher-ticket jobs, consumer and business financing provide flexible payment options.

Business Operations

Whether you need time tracking, reporting, accounting, or other features, Housecall Pro helps you run and grow your business. The platform’s AI Team provides access to specialized expertise, from coaches and customer service reps to analysts and marketers.

How To Choose the Right Software for Your Business

While intuitive and mobile-friendly, with strong reviews on G2 and Capterra, Housecall Pro may not offer everything that growing businesses or those with more specialized needs require. Before exploring Housecall Pro alternatives, it can be helpful to know what to look for in business management software. Here are a few questions to ask:

  • Team size: What’s more important: simplicity and low cost, or advanced dispatching, reporting, or call answering tools?
  • Industry needs: What are your specific needs — for example, inventory for HVAC or online booking for landscapers?
  • Mobile access: Do you have field technicians who need a mobile app?
  • Integrations: Do you require, for example, HVAC software compatible with QuickBooks, Stripe, or other tools?
  • Customer support: How is the onboarding, training, and responsiveness to support inquiries?
  • Scalability: Can the platform grow with you?

Housecall Pro Alternatives (With Pros and Cons)

Other companies like Housecall Pro are worth considering before you decide on a business management platform. Here’s our roundup of Housecall Pro alternatives to help you find the right fit.

1. ServiceTitan

Best for: Medium to large field service businesses that need detailed reporting, automation, and integration at scale

Key Features:

  • Advanced scheduling and dispatch board
  • Real-time reporting and analytics
  • Mobile app for field technicians
  • Built-in CRM with customer history tracking
  • Invoicing, estimates, and payment processing
  • Inventory and equipment management
  • Marketing and lead tracking tools
  • Integration with QuickBooks and other software

Pros:

  • Highly customizable and scalable
  • Powerful analytics and reporting tools
  • Strong support for multi-location operations

Cons:

  • Higher cost compared to other options
  • Some users report a steep learning curve
  • Contracts may include high cancellation fees

2. Jobber

Best for: Solo operators or small field service operators, such as landscapers, cleaners, HVAC technicians, and plumbers

Key features:

  • Client management tools
  • Scheduling and dispatching
  • Quoting and invoicing
  • Payment processing and tracking
  • Mobile access
  • Integration with QuickBooks Online

Pros:

  • Simple, intuitive interface
  • Quick setup and onboarding
  • Frequent feature updates

Cons:

  • Higher cost for advanced features
  • Limited accounting functionality
  • Some mobile features may be clunky

3. Workiz

Best for: Small to midsize field service businesses, including HVAC, plumbing, electrical, locksmith, junk removal, appliance repair, garage door, landscaping, and pest control services

Key features:

  • Client management tools
  • Scheduling and dispatching
  • Quoting and invoicing
  • Payment processing and tracking
  • Mobile access via the Workiz app
  • Integration with QuickBooks and other third-party tools

Pros:

  • User-friendly and customizable interface
  • Built-in phone system and SMS features
  • Helpful automation tools like AI Dispatcher

Cons:

  • Higher cost compared to other options
  • Some users report slow or inconsistent customer support
  • Certain features require a learning curve

4. FieldEdge

Best for: HVAC, plumbing, and other service businesses that need real-time visibility and QuickBooks integration

Key Features:

  • Scheduling and dispatching with a drag-and-drop interface
  • Real-time technician tracking and status updates
  • Mobile app for job access and invoicing in the field
  • Payment collection and invoicing from any device
  • QuickBooks integration for accurate, real-time accounting
  • Service history tracking and customer communication tools

Pros:

  • Strong dispatch tools with live technician tracking
  • Seamless QuickBooks integration
  • Helpful customer support team

Cons:

  • Interface can be buggy for some users
  • Reports lack advanced customization
  • May not be user-friendly in the field

5. Service Fusion

Best for: Solo to midsize service businesses that need affordable, all-in-one job management without per-user fees

Key features:

  • Scheduling and dispatching with drag-and-drop functionality
  • Estimates, invoicing, and payment processing
  • Mobile access for field technicians
  • Project management and job photo uploads
  • Inventory tracking and job costing
  • Integration with QuickBooks and other business tools

Pros:

  • Good value for money
  • Simple to onboard new users

Cons:

  • Some users report mobile app glitches
  • Fewer integrations than others
  • Potentially high cost for smaller teams

6. Meridian Local

Best for: Service businesses looking to combine job management with digital marketing and organic lead generation

Key features:

  • Integrated calendar and online booking
  • Estimates, billing, invoicing, and payment processing
  • Cloud-based CRM with contact and message tracking
  • Automated email and SMS messaging
  • Integrated inbox and business email management
  • E-commerce tools and merchant services
  • Website design, SEO, listings management, and digital advertising tools

Pros:

  • Expert marketing support and lead generation strategies
  • Dedicated account manager
  • No long-term contracts

Cons:

  • More marketing-focused than some alternatives
